title: Forces and Motion
summary: Newton's three laws in everyday words, with friction, gravity and inertia.

steps.title: What is a force?
sentences: A force is a push or a pull.
Forces can start something moving, stop it, speed it up or change its direction.
We measure force in a unit called the newton.

steps.title: Newton's first law
sentences: An object stays still, or keeps moving in a straight line at the same speed, unless a force acts on it.
That is why you lean forward when a bus suddenly brakes.
points: Things keep doing what they were doing

steps.title: Newton's second and third laws
sentences: The harder you push something, the faster it speeds up, and the heavier it is, the harder it is to push.
For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
When you push a wall, the wall pushes back on you.

steps.title: Gravity and friction
sentences: Gravity is the pull between objects, and on Earth it pulls everything toward the ground.
Friction is the force that slows things sliding over each other, and it is what lets us walk without slipping.
Without gravity and friction our everyday world would be very different.

facts: On the Moon you would weigh about one sixth of your weight on Earth, because its gravity is weaker.
In a vacuum a feather and a hammer fall together: astronauts showed this on the Moon in 1971.
Friction produces heat: rub your hands together to feel it.

options: The tendency to keep doing what it is doing
quiz.why: Inertia is resistance to changes in motion.

quiz.q: What force slows things sliding over each other?

quiz.why: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
